title: Two seedlings share a resource
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: Both have a cost relative to growing alone, so the model represents competition. Different environments can change competitive effects.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: Two seedlings compete for a limiting resource, and each grows less than it would alone in this model. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Seedling A and Seedling B, in that order? Seedling A: −; Seedling B: −. Both have a cost relative to growing alone, so the model represents competition. Different environments can change competitive effects.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Seedling A–Seedling B interaction as stated in the lesson? Both have a cost relative to growing alone, so the model represents competition. Different environments can change competitive effects.
